# Synthesis and Framing Bias

**Dimension:** Biases introduced during synthesis — narrative smoothing,
contradiction suppression, cherry-picking, hypothesis anchoring, and
confirmation bias in evaluation. These biases shape how retrieved information
is combined, framed, and presented to users.

All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Self-Contradiction in Synthesis

LLMs produce internally inconsistent outputs, generating claims in one part of
a response that contradict claims in another [38].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Self-contradiction rate (ChatGPT) | 17.7% | [38] |
| Detection F1 score | ~80% | [38] |

A 17.7% self-contradiction rate [38] means that synthesized research outputs
will regularly contain statements that undermine other statements in the same
document — without any signal to the reader that a contradiction exists.

## Cherry-Picking and Selective Presentation

Users interacting with LLM-based search report feeling that information is
selectively presented [50], and source coverage data confirms systematic
domain divergence [5].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| User perception | Felt "manipulated to only see one side" | [50] |
| Domain divergence (LLM-SEs vs traditional SEs) | 37% | [5] |
| Average URLs cited per response (LLM-SEs) | 4.3 | [5] |
| Average URLs cited per response (traditional SEs) | 10.3 | [5] |

Users reported that the system "selectively presented information" making them
feel "manipulated to only see one side" [50]. This perception is supported by
the structural finding that LLM-SEs cite fewer than half the sources of
traditional search engines (4.3 vs 10.3 URLs) and draw from a 37% divergent
domain pool [5].

## Citation Pattern Amplification

LLMs do not just reproduce human citation bias — they amplify it [6].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Median citation count gap (generated vs ground truth) | 1,326 higher | [6] |
| Overlap with actual citations | 7% | [6] |
| Models tested | GPT-4, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 | [6] |
| Papers analyzed | 166 (3,066 references) | [6] |

When generating references, LLMs select papers with a median citation count
1,326 higher than the papers authors actually cited [6]. Only 7% overlap with
ground truth citations [6]. In synthesis, this means the evidence base skews
toward established consensus and away from the specific, often less-cited
studies that constitute the actual evidentiary foundation.

## Confirmation Bias in Evaluation

When LLMs evaluate claims or evidence, prior framing dramatically shifts their
judgments [3][61].

| Scenario | Effect | Source |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Bug-free framing on GPT-4o-mini | Detection drops 93.5pp | [3] |
| Claude Code with adversarial context | 88% success rate | [3] |
| Evaluator confidence after reviewing incorrect AI answers | Increases | [61] |

Evaluators become more confident in incorrect AI answers after review [61],
creating a feedback loop: the AI produces a confident synthesis, the human
evaluator's confidence in it increases even when the synthesis is wrong, and
this evaluation may feed back into training data for the next generation of
models. Bug-free framing reduces vulnerability detection by up to 93.5
percentage points [3].

## RAG-Specific Synthesis Bias

Retrieval-Augmented Generation introduces bias patterns even when the
retrieval step is debiased [53].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| RAG accuracy: high-cited vs low-cited sources | 4.6 vs 4.2, p=0.49 (no significant difference) | [52] |
| Censored dataset effect | Still produces biased output | [53] |

One study found no significant accuracy difference between RAG using
highly-cited vs less-cited sources (p=0.49), and noted RAG "can help mitigate
disparities" [52]. However, even when datasets are explicitly censored to
remove biased content, RAG can still produce biased outputs through increased
model confidence [53], suggesting bias operates through the synthesis step's
confidence mechanisms rather than citation-count preference.

## Cognitive Bias Amplification

LLMs amplify cognitive biases compared to humans, and multi-agent systems can
develop emergent collective biases [37][51].

| Dimension | Finding | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| LLM vs human cognitive bias | LLMs show amplified bias in moral decisions | [37] |
| Multi-agent systems | Emergent collective bias formation | [51] |

LLMs amplify human cognitive biases rather than mitigating them, particularly
in moral decision-making contexts [37]. In multi-agent architectures — the
kind used in agentic research systems — collective biases emerge from agent
interaction that are not present in any individual agent [51].

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Cherry-picking subjectivity:** The user perception data [50] is
  qualitative. Whether users' feeling of being "manipulated" reflects actual
  selective presentation or reflects the inherent narrowing of any summary is
  not disambiguated.
- **Confirmation bias domain transfer:** The 93.5pp detection drop [3] is from
  security code review. Whether the same magnitude applies to research
  synthesis — where ground truth is often contested — is unknown.
- **RAG bias mechanism:** The finding that censored datasets still produce
  biased RAG output [53] lacks a detailed causal mechanism. Whether the bias
  enters through retrieval ranking, context window packing, or generation is
  not isolated.
- **Multi-agent emergence:** The collective bias finding [51] establishes the
  phenomenon but does not quantify the magnitude or identify which agent
  architectures are most susceptible.
- **Missing: contradiction suppression measurement.** While self-contradiction
  is measured at 17.7% [38], there is no cited study measuring how often LLMs
  suppress contradictions found in sources during synthesis — presenting a
  false consensus rather than acknowledging disagreement.
- **Missing: hypothesis anchoring in research.** No cited study directly
  measures how an initial research question or hypothesis frames the
  subsequent synthesis, though anchoring bias [4] and confirmation bias [3]
  data suggest the effect is substantial.
- **Evaluator feedback loop:** The finding that evaluators become more
  confident in incorrect AI answers [61] is identified but the long-term
  effect on model training through this feedback loop is not quantified.
